what: Pálvölgyi's heptagon and his appendix Theorem A.3 decided in Lean through OpenAI's classification, transported to formal-conjectures' statement of Graham's conjecture: the pre-registered questions H1–H6 and the corollary D, each read back from the runs.
undecided: The heptagon and Theorem A.3 are Dömötör Pálvölgyi's, with ChatGPT (arXiv:2609.23327, 2026-09-20; the appendix labelled unchecked by its author); the classification that decides them is OpenAI's (openai/math). This record decides, in Lean's kernel and four independent kernels, that the heptagon is not Ramsey, that formal-conjectures' statement of Graham's conjecture is false, and that Theorem A.3 holds as printed. It does not decide the "almost every" clause of A.3, the appendix's other theorems, the six-point case (others' Lean), or that OpenAI's and formal-conjectures' definitions capture the informal notions.

deviations.text: The prior-art review said Theorem A.3 had been checked by nobody. Read again before the reveal: wstrinz (Will Strinz) had certified one instance exactly on 16 October (three rational and four algebraically independent circle points, J2-F7 in wstrinz/spherical-ramsey) and uses A.3 by hand for half of a circle phase diagram. Corrected in a dated amendment: the first proof of A.3 as stated, and the first in Lean.

The library’s namespace was renamed for publication after the checks had run. The rename was checked to change the name and nothing else, and the build, the audit, Lean’s from-scratch check on all three roots, two second kernels, both verbatim checks and a planted variant were re-run on the published code.

The first export of the published run was void: it named the root file, which is not a Lake module, so it came out empty and both kernels “accepted 0 declarations”. It was stopped and recorded; the script now exports the two leaf modules and refuses an empty export.
The rules name leanchecker --paranoid; Lean v4.34.1 has no such mode, so the check rests on leanchecker --fresh and the four independent kernels.
